# Mutants the tests miss on Linux, each with the reason it cannot change
# behavior there. The `mutants` workflow fails when the mutants it misses
# differ from this list. A line is a mutant as `cargo mutants --list` names
# it, without its line and column, so a name that occurs twice in a file is
# listed once for each miss. The runner boots Linux 7.0 (Landlock ABI v8).

# Not built on Linux, or not with `experimental-intercept`, which the
# workflow enables. Each shares its name with a mutant in the code Linux
# builds, which the tests catch, so the workflow cannot leave these out
# without a line number.
crates/fsgate/src/bin/fsgate-broker.rs: replace intercept::run -> ExitCode with Default::default()
crates/fsgate/src/broker.rs: replace peer_uid -> io::Result<u32> with Ok(0)
crates/fsgate/src/broker.rs: replace peer_uid -> io::Result<u32> with Ok(1)
crates/fsgate/src/containment.rs: replace apply -> Result<Applied, GateError> with Ok(Default::default())
crates/fsgate/src/containment.rs: replace == with != in apply

# The Linux `apply` checks that a strict lock ended fully enforced. The
# mutant checks a best-effort one instead, which differs only on a kernel
# below Landlock ABI v3. `best_effort_lock_reports_library_only` catches it
# in the kernels job's boot without Landlock.
crates/fsgate/src/containment.rs: replace == with != in apply

# `LockPolicy::BestEffort` turned into the strict default differs only on a
# kernel below Landlock ABI v3. `best_effort_lock_reports_library_only`
# catches it without Landlock, and the macOS run catches it too.
crates/fsgate/src/lib.rs: replace <impl From<LockPolicy> for LockOptions>::from -> LockOptions with Default::default()

# `CAN_READ_PEER_UID` is true on Linux and macOS, so the guard is false
# without the mutant too.
crates/fsgate/src/broker.rs: replace match guard !CAN_READ_PEER_UID with false in ServeOptions::allowed_uids

# The access flags are distinct bits, so `^` builds the same set as `|`.
crates/fsgate/src/containment.rs: replace | with ^ in apply
crates/fsgate/src/bin/fsgate-broker/confine.rs: replace | with ^ in restrict
crates/fsgate/src/bin/fsgate-broker/confine.rs: replace | with ^ in restrict
crates/fsgate/src/bin/fsgate-broker/confine.rs: replace | with ^ in restrict

# The connection is never descriptor 3. std reopens a closed standard stream
# at startup, the broker opens at least one grant before the connection's
# socket pair, and the broker keeps the pair's lower number, so the worker's
# end is 5 or higher.
crates/fsgate/src/bin/fsgate-broker/confine.rs: replace > with >= in close_others_at_exec

# The ruleset is a hard requirement, so `restrict_self` fails before it can
# report a ruleset it did not enforce, and it sets `no_new_privs` itself.
# Both halves are false wherever it succeeds; the check guards against a
# change in the crate.
crates/fsgate/src/bin/fsgate-broker/confine.rs: replace || with && in restrict

# The message for a kernel without Landlock ABI v3, which the runner's is
# not. `the_broker_refuses_to_start_a_worker_without_landlock` checks it in
# the kernels job's boot without Landlock.
crates/fsgate/src/bin/fsgate-broker/confine.rs: replace unavailable -> String with String::new()
crates/fsgate/src/bin/fsgate-broker/confine.rs: replace unavailable -> String with "xyzzy".into()
